primary_citation: Cal. Penal Code §§630-638 (California Invasion of Privacy Act; Stats. 1967, Ch. 1509; §632.7 current version Stats. 2016, Ch. 541)
short_title: California Invasion of Privacy Act (CIPA) — All-Party Consent; Civil Remedy $5,000/Violation
one_line_rule: California requires consent of all parties before recording or intercepting any confidential communication; cellular/cordless interceptions prohibited without all-party consent regardless of confidentiality; civil remedy is the greater of actual damages or $5,000 per violation, with discretionary trebling.

case_law.key_rule: Confidential communication under §632(c) = objective circumstances test; telephone calls made without knowledge of recording are presumptively confidential; content sensitivity does not determine confidentiality.

case_law.cite: Kearney v. Salomon Smith Barney, Inc., 39 Cal.4th 95 (2006)
case_law.key_rule: CIPA has extraterritorial reach; California all-party consent rule protects California residents even when the recording/intercepting party is located in a one-party consent state. Interceptor's location does not defeat California CIPA coverage when victim is a California resident.

sim_swap_application.primary_provision: Cal. Penal Code §632.7 — cellular interception without all-party consent; no confidentiality showing required
sim_swap_application.secondary_provision: Cal. Penal Code §631 — wire interception; reading communications in transit; disclosure of intercepted content
sim_swap_application.civil_remedy: §637.2: $5,000 per violation (each intercepted communication = separate violation) OR 3× actual damages (discretionary trebling)
sim_swap_application.federal_stack: Federal §2511 ($10,000 minimum) + California §632.7 ($5,000 minimum) = $15,000 minimum per interception event; federal also provides mandatory attorneys' fees
sim_swap_application.disclosure_chain: §631(b): each person who received and used intercepted communications = separate violation; Christina Cerretani and others in the disclosure chain = $5,000 minimum per disclosure
sim_swap_application.extraterritoriality: Kearney establishes California CIPA applies regardless of where McClaran was located when conducting SIM swap; Michael's California residency controls
sim_swap_application.sol: CCP §335.1 (2 years from discovery); each interception event = separate violation with own SOL; discovery rule tolling for period victim unaware of interception
sim_swap_application.defendants: Ryan McClaran (interceptor §632.7/§631); Christina Cerretani and others (§631(b) disclosure); AT&T (UCL §17200 predicate from enabling SIM swap)
